description:
## Finding

`ChatBackend::generate_invite_code`'s rustdoc at
`crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:362-365` says:

```
/// 2. **Minimum 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy.** The default
///    implementation here emits 32 lowercase-hex characters
///    (16 bytes = 128 bits) which is the workspace floor.
///    Production backends MAY use more; less is forbidden.
```

The phrase "The default implementation here emits …" suggests
the trait method carries a default body that does the
described thing. The actual signature at line 414 is:

```
fn generate_invite_code(&self) -> String;
```

— terminating semicolon, **no default body**. The "default
implementation" the rustdoc names does not exist on the trait;
it lives only on the reference `MemoryBackend` in `memory.rs`.

## What goes wrong for a reader

A consumer reading the doc on docs.rs sees a positive claim that
the trait method has a default impl returning a 32-char
lowercase-hex string. They could:

1. **Skip implementing the method**, assuming the default is
   adequate for a stub backend. Result: compile error (the
   method is abstract). Mildly annoying, not a contract bug.

2. **Trust the description as authoritative**, conclude "the
   default emits 16 bytes", and implement THEIR backend to do
   the same — fine.

3. **Skim the doc and conclude this is a `Has-A-Default` method**
   when assessing the trait surface, miscount the required-to-
   implement vs. has-default-impl methods, and budget testing
   incorrectly.

The third failure mode is the one that bites real implementers.
The first compiles-fail and is self-correcting.

## Why this is a real finding, not a typo

There's a parallel stale note in `invite.rs:210-213` saying:

> default implementation is nanosecond-seeded and NOT
> cryptographically secure

referring to a default that no longer exists. Two separate doc
comments reference a default-impl that the trait does not have.
This is structural drift between the rustdoc and the trait, not
a one-off typo.

The history hint: an earlier revision of the trait apparently
had a default impl on `generate_invite_code` (the `invite.rs`
warning makes that clear — the original default WAS nanosecond-
seeded). It was removed at some point, with the surrounding doc
left unedited.

## Recommendation

Rewrite the rustdoc bullet to refer to the reference
implementation, not "the default implementation here":

> 2. **Minimum 128 bits of CSPRNG entropy.** The reference
>    `MemoryBackend` impl in this crate emits 32 lowercase-hex
>    characters (16 bytes = 128 bits) which is the workspace
>    floor. Production backends MAY use more; less is forbidden.

And delete the stale paragraph at `invite.rs:210-213` referring
to the never-existent default. Both changes are doc-only.

## Engineering basis

- `backend.rs:362-365` and `backend.rs:414` read directly.
- `invite.rs:210-213` read for the parallel stale reference.
- No default-impl block exists in the trait
  (`backend.rs:295-893`); a full read of the trait body
  confirms the signature at line 414 terminates with `;`.

## Priority justification

P3 because:
- The misstatement is small.
- The natural failure modes are compile-fail-self-correcting
  (mode 1) or just-implement-the-same-thing (mode 2).
- The doc-as-contract surface concern (mode 3) is real but
  bounded.

The 4th-pass api-contract supplement explicitly flagged
"running out of real complaints" territory. This is a real
finding (the rustdoc factually misstates the trait shape), but
it is small. Including for completeness; reviewer welcome to
downgrade to opinion if they weight the cost differently.

## Cross-reference

JMAP-x2gd.67 marked "N2 (MUST-override prose contracts, footgun
ID generator)" as mail-server-LOCAL. The current finding is a
chat-server-specific stale-default-reference doc bug, not a
generalization of N2; the two findings are distinct.
title: API contract: generate_invite_code rustdoc references 'the default implementation here emits 32 lowercase-hex characters' but the trait method has no default impl
